previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of mesenteric fibromatosis and recurrent small bowel obstructions was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain consistent with prior flares. Imaging showed no mechanical obstruction, and symptoms were managed with NPO status, TPN, IV fluids, and pain and nausea control using IV Dilaudid and rectal morphine and Phenergan. She was advanced to clear liquids but redeveloped vomiting after attempting a regular diet, prompting reversion to clear liquids at discharge with instructions to advance slowly at home. A tear in the femoral TPN line hub was repaired via nonoperative intervention, and ethanol locks were initiated. Her chronic conditions, including migraines, hypothyroidism, anemia of chronic disease, and asthma, remained stable. She was discharged home on a clear liquid diet with updated PR medications for pain and nausea, instructions to resume TPN, and plans for outpatient follow-up.

# FEVER: Patient reported fever to 100.5 noted incidentally on 
temperature check at home, afebrile since arrival to ED (>24 
hours). No other clinical e/o SIRS. Appeared non-toxic on exam. 
Labs notable for relative leukocytosis to 10.4 (WNL, but 
significantly elevated since ___ when count was 2.8), improved 
to 5.6 on HD #2. She had slight erythema over her right groin 
TPN site, which could suggest cellulitis or line infection 
(elevated risk for this given TPN infusions), although erythema 
is extremely minor and not a/w fluctuance, warmth, or exudate. 
UTI was considered given h/o frequent UTIs, although denied 
dysuria; UA fairly bland (few bacteria, 11 WBCs) and urine 
culture negative. Pneumonia extremely unlikely since denies 
cough or dyspnea and completely benign lung exam. Blood cultures 
(peripheral and from indwelling femoral line) and urine cultures 
were obtained and are pending on discharge (no growth to date). 
After she had remained afebrile for two days, she was discharged 
to home. 
  
# ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY: Creatinine elevated to 1.2 on admission, 
baseline 0.8-0.9. Likely pre-renal insufficiency secondary to 
chronic nausea and vomiting. Improved to 0.9 with IV fluids, 
supporting this hypothesis. 
  
# ERYTHEMA AT RIGHT FEMORAL TPN LINE SITE: site appeared mildly 
irritated and minimally erythematous; no discharge or fluctuance 
and did not look like a cellulitis. Pt reports that she has ___ 
pain during infusions through the line. She had tube study on 
___ which showed no leak in tunneled portion of line. A tear 
in the outer portion was repaired. Could be some new/residual 
tear or inflammation around the line which is causing pain. 
Emailed IV nurse ___ (has managed patient's femoral 
line issues in past) who recommended repeat line study in the 
near future but does not need to happen as inpatient. She will 
follow up as outpatient for this study.

was found not to be obstructed on imaging. Symptoms were managed 
with PR morphine and IV dilaudid for breakthrough, IV phenergan 
for nausea. Currently reports pain is unchanged since last 
discharge, feels that PR morphine and PR phenergan may have been 
leaking out of her rectum which is why they are not helping very

IV q8 hrs PRN for breakthrough pain.
